diagnosis: Writes the full sum of the ones place beside the sum of the tens place instead of regrouping ten ones into a ten.
rationale: The student computed 3 + 2 = 5 and 7 + 6 = 13, concatenating them to get 513 instead of regrouping 10 ones into 1 ten. Demonstrating make-a-ten with a collection of ones (like 14 ones) shows bundling ten ones into one ten.

script.focus: ten ones bundling into one ten

intent: Demonstrate make-a-ten on the place-value with values [14]. Tutor points at: ten ones bundling into one ten

frames.caption: Here are 14 ones. That is too many for the ones place: it can only hold 0 to 9.
Bundle ten of them. Ten ones make one ten, so the bundle moves to the tens place. 4 ones are left.
Write 1 in the tens place and 4 in the ones place: 14. One digit per place.

judgement.reasoning: The student wrote 513 for 37 + 26 because they do not understand that the ones column cannot hold a two-digit number and must be regrouped. The demo explicitly explains that the ones place can only hold digits 0-9 and visually shows bundling 10 ones into 1 ten, perfectly addressing the root misconception with an easier worked demonstration without spoiling the exact problem (37 + 26).
judgement.verdict: A teacher would definitely use this detour right now because it directly explains why 14 (analogous to the student's 13) cannot sit entirely in the ones place.
